sentences.text: Unknown vs Haridas on 12 July, 2024

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  12.07.2024 C482 No. 457 of 2022  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.

1. Mr. Prabhat Bohra, learned counsel for the applicant through V.C. and Mr. Pratiroop Pandey,
learned AGA for the State.

2. By the present C482 Application, the applicant is challenging the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 330 of 2021, State Vs. Haridas, arising out of FIR dated 28.11.2019, bearing FIR No. 0491 of 2019, P.S. Rishikesh, District Dehradun for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467 and 120B of IPC.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the applicant and opposite party No. 2 entered into a partnership firm, in the name and style of "M/s M.D. Enterprises" through a registered partnership deed dated 11.12.2015 and in this regard, an account was opened in the name of the firm M/s M.D. Enterprises at Bank of Baroda, Birpur Khurd, Rishikesh, bearing Account No. 48410200000053.

Subsequently,
due to some differences between the partners, the partnership firm was dissolved on 20.02.2018.

4. On 13.11.2018, a cheque No. 00186 of Rs. 56,305/- was issued to one M/s Shadi Card Emporium through its proprietor Manoj Kumar and the cheque was dishonoured on 15.11.2018 with remarks "Funds Insufficient".

Thereafter, M/s Shadi Card Emporium filed a complaint under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act in the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh, District Dehradun, which was registered as Complaint Case No. 61 of 2019, M/s Shadi Card Emporium Vs. M/s M.D.
Enterprises through its partner Ms. Manju (applicant herein) and Deepak (Opposite party No.
2/complainant herein).
5.

Subsequently, the said proceedings initiated under Section 138 of the N.I. Act was compounded by invoking powers conferred under Section 147 of the N.I. Act, on the ground that a settlement has been arrived between the parties and the complainant received the cheque amount.

6. Subsequently, the Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh, District Dehradun closed the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 61 of 2019 and the applicant as well as the complainant herein, who were the accused in Complaint Case No. 61 of 2019 were acquitted under Section 147 of N.I. Act read with Unknown vs Haridas on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136249283/
1 Section 320(8) of CrPC by order dated 13.07.2019.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that despite the fact that the proceedings under Section 138 of N.I. Act was dropped by allowing the compounding application and both of them i.e. the applicant and respondent/complainant were acquitted on 13.07.2019, with an ulterior purpose and motive, the complainant/respondent No. 2, who himself was one of the accused along with the present applicant in Complaint Case No. 61 of 2019, lodged a First Information Report on 28.11.2019, implicating the present applicant for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 465 of IPC, in which after investigation, the chargesheet was filed for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 120B of IPC.
8.
On the said chargesheet, after taking cognizance the applicant was summoned by order dated 02.09.2021 in Criminal Case No. 330 No. 2021, State Vs. Haridas and another.

9. It is submitted that initiation of this proceeding pursuant to the FIR lodged by the respondent is glaring example of abuse of process of law since after compounding of the offence under Section 138 of N.I. Act, deliberately the FIR has been lodged by the respondent/complainant.

10. I found force on the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and the conduct of the complainant/respondent appears to be very surprising and prima facie establishes that with some ulterior purpose and motive, he initiated the criminal proceedings by lodging the First Information Report and this Court is also of the view that the investigating agency also conducted the investigation in a very casual manner and without any substance and material, the chargesheet has been filed.
11. Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, learned AGA accepts notice for respondent No. 1.

12. Issue Notice to respondent No.
2.
13.
Learned counsel for the applicant shall take steps to serve respondent within a week, returnable within three weeks by registered post, with acknowledgement due.
14. Respondents may file counter affidavit within four weeks.
Thereafter, two weeks' time is granted to the applicant to file rejoinder affidavit.

15. List this matter on 28.08.2024.
16.

Till further orders, the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 330 of 2021, arising out of FIR dated 28.11.2019, bearing FIR No. 0491 of 2019, P.S. Rishikesh, District Dehradun, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh, District Dehradun, shall remain stayed.
